key_insight: DFT-trained machine-learning surrogates efficiently predict small-polaron hopping dynamics and conductivity in the battery anode material Li₄Ti₅O₁₂ (LTO).
engineering_relevance: The workflow reduces the computational cost of evaluating charge transport in defective energy materials; the demonstrated application is a battery anode, not a solar cell.
method: Use DFT to calculate selected small-polaron hopping barriers.
Train ML surrogates to estimate barriers across many polaron configurations.
Feed predictions into a kinetic model to estimate conductivity.
evidence_signal: Using 154 of 3,649 symmetry-inequivalent barrier calculations, the workflow achieved over 20-fold computational efficiency and predicted room-temperature conductivity of 6.7 × 10⁻³ S/cm, within the experimental range.
watch_item: Transferability beyond the studied LTO conditions requires validation on other materials and defect configurations.
paper_title: A Machine-learning-aided Workflow for Sampling Small Polaron Dynamics in Energy Materials
